You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module specifies a simple concurrent algorithm in which N processes, numbered 0 through N−1 and conceptually arranged in a circle, each execute two sequential steps. In step `a`, process `i` writes 1 into shared array `x` at index `i`. In step `b`, it reads `x` at the left-neighbor index `(i−1) mod N` and writes that value into shared array `y` at index `i`. All processes begin at label `a`, and the PlusCal translation produces variables `x`, `y` (both initialized to all-zeros arrays over {0,1}), and a program-counter array `pc` tracking each process's current label among `{"a", "b", "Done"}`. The constant `N` is assumed to be a positive natural number; the model-checking configuration fixes it to 5.

The core correctness property, `PCorrect`, asserts that when all processes have terminated, at least one process `i` has `y[i] = 1`. The module proves `Spec => []PCorrect` using TLAPS by establishing an inductive invariant `Inv`, which combines type-correctness (`TypeOK`) with two additional conjuncts: that any process past label `a` has already set `x[i] = 1`, and that either some process has not yet finished or some `y[i]` is already 1. Two TLAPS theorems (`Correctness` and `Correctness2`) formally verify this invariance, the latter being a more concise proof accepted by the same proof system. TLC is also configured to check `PCorrect`, `TypeOK`, and `Inv` as invariants against the specification.
